report.answer_text:
In 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed what she called “responsible and proactive” fiscal policy: use government spending and tax relief to ease the cost-of-living squeeze, while investing with the private sector to raise wages and strengthen long-term growth. She laid out the approach in her October 24 policy speech, and her Cabinet approved a ¥21.3 trillion stimulus package on November 21. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
Her main proposals were:
Cut household costs. Scrap the provisional gasoline and diesel tax surcharges, subsidize winter electricity and gas bills, provide extra payments to families with children, and give local governments funds to help residents cope with higher food prices. (mof.go.jp)
Raise take-home pay. Raise the minimum taxable income threshold to ¥1.78 million in the fiscal 2026 tax plan, begin designing a refundable tax credit for low- and middle-income earners, and help small businesses afford wage increases. Her October coalition agreement also called for considering a two-year suspension of the consumption tax on qualifying food and beverages; that was not part of the November stimulus. (mof.go.jp)
Invest in strategic industries and economic security. Direct public and private investment toward areas such as AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, quantum technology, and space, while strengthening critical supply chains, energy and food security, and disaster preparedness. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
The Diet passed a separate ¥18.3 trillion supplementary budget on December 16 to fund much of the package. The two figures measure different things: the broader stimulus total also counted measures such as tax cuts. (japan.kantei.go.jp)

quotes.text: We will expand our provision of grants to local regions for prioritized assistance, aimed at assisting local governments.
We will create a menu of recommended measures that provide support for consumers impacted by high prices
we will provide assistance for electricity and gas bills during the winter months when the cold is most severe.
We will strongly support wage increases and capital investment through means such as assistance to boost productivity
Strategic investments that enhance resilience against potential crises are the core focus of the Takaichi Cabinet's growth strategy.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back spending-based cost-of-living aid (energy bill help, consumer support) and wage and capital investment support for growth, but nothing mentions tax relief or investing with the private sector.
pages.page_reason: The page describes strategic fiscal policy to raise incomes and boost revenues, measures for rising prices including supplementary budget, tax relief such as raising the dependent deduction limit and refundable tax credits, support for SMEs and wage increases, and strategic public-private investments for growth, so it covers all parts of the claim.

quotes.text: We will advance public-private partnership investment in strategic sectors—such as AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, quantum technologies, fusion, drug discovery, biotechnology, aviation, and space—and strengthen supply chains for critical materials.
From the perspective of ensuring food security, we will embark on five years of intensive measures to transform agricultural structures
To build an economic and social structure resilient to rising energy costs, we will press forward with the restarting of nuclear reactors
We will steadily promote initiatives intended to boost national resilience in line with relevant plans, while enhancing and reinforcing our disaster management system

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state strengthening supply chains for critical materials, food security measures through agricultural transformation and energy resilience through nuclear restarts, and enhancing disaster management, so every element of the claim is backed.
pages.page_reason: The page explicitly mentions strengthening supply chains for critical materials, establishing food security, strengthening energy and resource security, and promoting disaster prevention and national resilience, which together cover all parts of the claim.
